summary: The Sunfolk Steadings: a realm of men among the tall Sunhot realms, farmers, caravan-men and spear-carriers for hire, who may win a guest's seat at Noon.

steward_of_goodin.name: The Steward of Goodin
steward_of_goodin.desc: Odun keeps the steadings' common granary and the steadings' common law. He is a head shorter than any Speaker he meets, and does not seem to notice.

steadings_endure.name: The Steadings Endure
steadings_endure.desc: Each steading keeps its fields, its fences and its feud, and all of them keep the common law. The steadings have survived neighbours twice their height and four times their age.

tall_folks_trust.name: The Tall Folk's Trust
tall_folks_trust.desc: Sunhot merchants talk to Goodin's traders as to equals, and Sunhot families send their sons to the steadings to learn how men farm. The trust was earned slowly and is kept carefully.

sunfolk_caravans.name: Caravans of the Sunfolk
sunfolk_caravans.desc: Goodin's caravans cross the Lands of the Sun with grain, wool and the news, and the caravan-men are welcome at every inn. A Sunfolk wagon is easy to know by its low wheels.

spear_companies.name: The Spear Companies
spear_companies.desc: The Sunfolk hire out their spears by the season, in companies of fifty with a captain and a banner. Each company has its own song, and each song has a rude verse.

guest_seat_request.title: The Sunfolk Ask for a Guest's Seat
guest_seat_request.desc: Steward Odun's envoys stand in the white hall, a head shorter than the Speakers, and ask that the Sunfolk be allowed to sit at the Noon Council as guests. They ask for no vote, no chair and no name on the roll.

options.name: The Council is for the Sunhot realms
Let the Sunfolk sit as guests

focuses.name: The Sunfolk Steadings
focuses.desc: Goodin is a realm of men among the Sunhot realms: the steadings of the Sunfolk, led by a Steward and a moot of steading-heads. Its neighbours are more than a head taller, and the Sunfolk are proud of it.

focuses.name: The Steward
focuses.desc: Odun is the Steward of the steadings, chosen by the moot for his patience and his fair hand. He holds the common seal and the common key.

focuses.name: The Steading Moot
focuses.desc: The heads of the steadings meet in a barn at harvest, each with a sack of his own grain. Whoever has the biggest sack speaks first and listens longest.

focuses.name: Sunfolk Customs
focuses.desc: The Sunfolk have their own customs, written down by an old steader in a book of soft grey cloth. They are the customs of men who live among giants.

focuses.name: The Sunfolk Way
focuses.desc: The way of the Sunfolk is to work, to keep faith and to ask for nothing that is not owed. Their banner is plain brown, and they carry it with pride.

focuses.name: The Steadings Endure
focuses.desc: A great granary is built at the heart of the steadings, and every steading adds a tithe each harvest. The Sunfolk will not starve while it stands.

focuses.name: Men Among the Tall
focuses.desc: The Sunfolk live beside neighbours who are a head taller and many centuries older. They have learned to be courteous, patient and very hard to move.

focuses.name: Gifts to the Lands of Light
focuses.desc: The Steward sends the Radiant Speaker a gift of barley, honey and well-made tools. The Lands of Light accepts with a graceful letter.

focuses.name: A Guest's Seat at Noon
focuses.desc: The Noon Council is for the Sunhot realms, but the Sunfolk would like to listen. The Steward writes a respectful petition for a guest's seat.

focuses.name: Neighbours of Goodton and Guuden
focuses.desc: Goodton and Guuden are realms of men too, and their steadings border the Sunfolk's. The three hold a council of neighbours in a field between them.

focuses.name: Sunfolk and Sunhot
focuses.desc: Sunfolk and Sunhot sit at the same table, though the benches are of different heights. The tall folk have learned that men can be reliable neighbours.

focuses.name: The Tall Folk's Trust
focuses.desc: The trust of the Sunhot realms is slow in coming and slow in going. The Sunfolk have earned it, and mean to keep it.

focuses.name: Caravans of the Sunfolk
focuses.desc: Goodin's caravan-men cross the Lands of the Sun with grain, wool and the news. A Sunfolk wagon is known by its low wheels and its good brakes.

focuses.name: Markets Beyond the Sun
focuses.desc: The caravan-men carry news of new markets beyond the borders, and the Steward sends agents to see them. Some return richer, and some do not return at all.

focuses.name: Hired Spears of Goodin
focuses.desc: The Sunfolk hire out their spears by the season, in companies of fifty with a captain and a banner. They are paid by the day and discharged by the month.

focuses.name: Sunfolk Bows
focuses.desc: Sunfolk archers use short bows of ash and horn, built for a man who stands behind a hedge. They shoot very quickly and very straight.

focuses.name: The Spear Companies
focuses.desc: Each company has its own song, and each song has a rude verse. They muster at the Steward's call, in rows of six, and their captains know each man by name.

focuses.name: Captains of the Sunfolk
focuses.desc: The best company captains are gathered in the Steward's hall to teach their craft. The Sunfolk have a name for steadiness, and these are the men who earned it.
